verdict: Illinois Tool Works grew revenue 4% to $4.24B and posted record operating income of $1.18B — a 27.8% margin — even though a tornado knocked out two welding plants for part of the quarter.

segments.name: Test & Measurement and Electronics
segments.note: Testing instruments and electronics equipment — the fastest grower, up 17% on capital-spending demand.

segments.name: Automotive OEM
segments.note: Fasteners and components sold to car makers. Shown net of $4M of sales between ITW's own segments.

segments.name: Food Equipment
segments.note: Commercial ovens, dishwashers and refrigeration for restaurants and institutions — ITW's highest-profile steady business.

segments.name: Welding
segments.note: Welding equipment — grew 7% despite a tornado damaging two plants in late July; without it, growth would have been about 15%.

segments.name: Polymers & Fluids
segments.note: Adhesives, sealants and fluids for industry.

segments.name: Construction Products
segments.note: Fasteners and tools for building and renovation.

segments.name: Specialty Products
segments.note: A collection of niche product lines, from airport equipment to appliance components.

opex.name: Selling, administrative & R&D
opex.note: Selling, administration and product development across ITW's seven decentralized segments.

opex.name: Amortization & impairment of intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of past acquisitions over time.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $83M, partly offset by $37M of other income.

takeaways.title: Margins keep expanding
takeaways.text: Operating margin rose 40 basis points to 27.8% — price increases beat rising raw-material costs, and ITW's enterprise initiatives added about 130 basis points.

takeaways.title: A tornado dented the top line
takeaways.text: Late-July tornado damage at two Welding plants cost an estimated $40M of revenue; business-interruption insurance covered most of the lost profit.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised again
takeaways.text: Full-year GAAP EPS guidance was narrowed to $11.45–$11.55 (midpoint $11.50, +10%), and the dividend was raised for the 63rd consecutive year.

oneTimers: Tornado damage to two Welding facilities in late July reduced revenue by an estimated $40M; the lost operating income was largely offset by business interruption insurance.
